source_text: Triplicem philosophiam Salomon in tribus libris tradidisse putandus est: ethicam in Proverbiis, physicam in Ecclesiasten, epopticen sive contemplativam in Cantico Canticorum. In Proverbiis mores corriguntur; in Ecclesiasten vanitas creaturarum ostenditur; in Cantico Canticorum ad unionem Verbi et sponsae contemplatio perducit. Idem ordo apud Graecos: prius ethica, deinde physica, ad ultimum epoptica.

pass_b_english: Solomon is to be thought to have handed down a threefold philosophy in three books: ethics in Proverbs, physics in Ecclesiastes, epoptics or contemplation in the Song of Songs. In Proverbs morals are corrected; in Ecclesiastes the vanity of creatures is shown; in the Song of Songs contemplation leads to the union of the Word and the Bride. The same order among the Greeks: first ethics, then physics, and last epoptics.
